title: Licensing and Source Header Contract
readerIntent: Preserve the repository's canonical source header and avoid inconsistent generated or handwritten legal text.
owner: Repository license agreement and Nodics copyright-quality/generation contracts
summary: Every Nodics-owned handwritten, generated, template, and customer-skeleton JavaScript source uses the same tooling-owned 2026 header; documentation explains enforcement but does not grant or reinterpret legal rights.

sections.heading: Legal boundary
paragraphs: The applicable repository distribution and license agreement controls use, modification, and redistribution. This page is an engineering consistency contract, not legal advice and not an additional license grant. Ask the authorized Nodics legal or repository owner when rights or obligations are unclear.

sections.heading: Files covered
items: Generated JavaScript source and regenerated artifacts.
JavaScript templates and module/project skeleton files.
Customer project JavaScript skeletons generated by Nodics tooling.
JavaScript snippets presented as complete Nodics source/template examples.

sections.heading: Rules
items: Use the canonical 2026 Nodics source header supplied and validated by repository tooling.
Do not hand-edit one file, module, provider, template, or generated artifact to use alternate copyright years, spelling, ownership, or legal wording.
When the canonical text changes, update the tooling copyright quality service, shared header utility, structure/module generators, templates, tests, documentation, and regenerated artifacts together.
Markdown pages do not require the JavaScript block header at the top; repository-owned metadata/data formats follow their governing file contract.
Third-party source, notices, generated vendor code, and dependencies retain their applicable upstream licenses and must not be relabeled as Nodics-owned code.
Do not remove attribution, notices, or license files without explicit legal/repository-owner approval.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Run `npm run quality:copyright` to detect missing, duplicated, malformed, or stale Nodics JavaScript headers.
Use `npm run quality:copyright:fix` only for the repository-governed normalization it supports, then review the complete diff.
Regenerate templates/artifacts through their owner rather than manually correcting every output.
Run structure, documentation, generated-context, focused, and regression gates affected by header/tooling changes.
A clean header check proves format consistency; it does not prove third-party license compatibility or resolve legal questions.
